notes: Play knowledge rewritten as executable actions. Every reference is checked against the generated level data by tools/gen_level_nuance.py.
Streets is the level where the player's most powerful weapon is also the fastest way to fail: the tank makes the route survivable and its main gun kills the civilians the mission requires be spared.

nuance.claim: The pursuit is done in the tank rather than on foot; the streets are long and open and the tank is what makes crossing them survivable.
The tank's explosive shell kills civilians in a wide radius, so the mission is driven rather than shot; the gun is the single biggest cause of failing the casualty objective.
nuance.because: Objective 2 is a standing casualty constraint that runs for the whole level, and the tank shell is the only wide-radius weapon available.

nuance.claim: Civilians share the streets with the soldiers throughout, so there is no stretch of the level where undirected fire is safe.
Driving through crowds runs civilians down and counts against the casualty objective just as shooting them does, so the tank is steered around them.
Contacting Valentin is only required above Agent, and his dialogue delays the pursuit, so it is done before the chase rather than during it.
nuance.because: Objective 0 carries a minimum difficulty above Agent while objective 1 does not.

nuance.claim: Valentin is found off the main route through the back alleys, so reaching him means deliberately leaving the road the pursuit follows.
The contact completes through dialogue, so the objective needs the player to hold position until Valentin has finished speaking.
Reaching the gate at the end of the pursuit ends the mission, so nothing can be collected afterwards.
nuance.because: Objective 1 is the level exit; unfinished objectives score as failed.
